audit.title: Automation Billing and Costs

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Working: "Chainlink Automation requires only an execution fee for transactions onchain." is a clean liftable opener. Weak: the two formula panels live inside `TabsContent`/`Fragment` MDX components that may not render as retrievable text — the canonical fee formula risks being invisible to a crawler.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 9 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, median 76 words/section, none over 600. Chunk boundaries are clean.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong; the worked example (110,051 gas, 182,723,799,380 wei, 0.008077 LINK) is exactly the high-lift content engines cite. Minor drag from vague quantifiers ("last several blocks," "next few blocks," "fast gas price").

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak; 4 external links but 0 to primary sources. ERC-677 and ERC-20 are named without linking their specs; the LINK/Native rate is "fetched from Chainlink Oracle" without a data-feeds link.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Adequate; the fee-composition sentence is quotable, but "ERC-677 LINK" gets a usage note, not a one-sentence definition near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak; measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak; 0 fenced blocks. The formulas and the final arithmetic (`0.008077 = [...]`) are prose/MDX, not language-tagged blocks an agent can parse or copy.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Adequate; lifecycle is covered (cost → fund → withdraw → minimum balance → gas), but there's no FAQ/troubleshooting and no symptom-phrased headings ("Why isn't my upkeep being performed?").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Good, but the withdrawal examples slip into first person: "I will receive 5 LINK" — inconsistent voice that weakens entity/agent parsing.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured billing reference: the fee formula, a fully worked Polygon example with real gas/wei values, and clean section boundaries make most of it highly extractable. Its single biggest strength is concrete specificity (42 numerals per 1k words, a real onchain transaction cited). Its biggest opportunity is metadata and retrieval framing — zero JSON-LD, missing canonical URL, no visible date, and concept-titled sections that don't match the symptom/cost questions developers actually type. Honest verdict: strong content, under-optimized for how engines discover and trust it.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no date signals.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential `url`; add a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and schema are E-E-A-T signals engines use to select and trust sources for factual pricing answers.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.issue: headings like "No node competition," "Minimum balance" don't match user queries.
recommendations.change: Add H2/H3 or FAQ entries phrased as "How much does Chainlink Automation cost?", "Why isn't my upkeep being performed?" (→ minimum balance), "Why was I charged a 0.1 LINK cancellation fee?", "How do I withdraw upkeep funds?"
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by symptom and question; concept-titled prose loses retrieval it would otherwise win.

recommendations.title: Ensure the fee formula renders as plain extractable text
recommendations.issue: canonical formula is trapped in MDX tab components.
recommendations.change: Precede the tabs with a plain-text canonical statement of both LINK and native fee formulas (or render formulas in a fenced/code block) so the answer survives chunking.
recommendations.why: if the formula isn't in liftable text, engines answer from priors instead of the page's canonical math.

recommendations.title: Put the fee arithmetic in a labeled code block
recommendations.change: Wrap the formula and substituted-values calculation in a fenced block; consider a small runnable snippet computing the fee.
recommendations.why: structured, tagged calculations are easier to parse, quote, and reproduce.

recommendations.title: Link primary/canonical references
recommendations.where: "ERC-677 LINK" section and the oracle rate mention
recommendations.issue: 0 links to primary sources; ERC-677/ERC-20 unlinked.
recommendations.change: Link ERC-677 and ERC-20 to their EIP specs, and link "Chainlink Oracle"/rate to the relevant Data Feeds doc.
recommendations.why: inline authoritative links raise citation rate and credibility.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics
recommendations.issue: "last several blocks," "next few blocks," "fast gas price."
recommendations.change: State the actual block window / percentile target and define "fast gas price" (e.g. the source feed), even if approximate/configurable.
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; vague qualifiers underperform.

recommendations.title: Fix first-person voice in withdrawal examples
recommendations.change: Use second person: "you will receive 5 LINK."
recommendations.why: consistent voice aids clean extraction and reads as authoritative reference.

recommendations.title: Add a one-sentence ERC-677 definition near first use
recommendations.issue: term used throughout, defined only via PegSwap workaround.
recommendations.change: Open with "ERC-677 LINK is the transferAndCall-capable LINK token required to fund upkeeps; ERC-20 LINK must be converted first."
recommendations.why: a crisp definition near first use is verbatim-liftable.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "many," "several," "fast" flagged in measured facts.
Formula content locked in MDX tab components — risk of non-rendered/unretrievable canonical text.
First-person voice ("I will receive") inconsistent with reference-doc register.
No stale-content evidence, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no undifferentiated walls.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; confirm this page is indexed there.
Canonical URL, JSON-LD, and freshness cadence are partly template/site-level; ensure the docs platform emits them site-wide rather than page-by-page.
Head metadata could not be verified from the supplied content — pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
